name: @nkc27/life-admin-mcp

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Where the life-admin folder lives and what it holds: item counts by type, how many are overdue and how many are due in the next 30 days. Call once at the start of a conversation to orient.

tools.name: list_items
tools.description: List tracked items, optionally filtered by type, sorted by due date (undated items last).

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Full details of one item by title: provider, cost, due date with days left and when reminders start, reference, and its notes and history.

tools.name: search_items
tools.description: Find items whose title, provider, tags or notes contain any of the words in the query, best matches first. Use before add_item to avoid duplicates, and for questions like 'where's the boiler warranty?'.

tools.name: due_soon
tools.description: What needs attention: overdue items, items due within the next `days` days, and items further out whose reminder window has already opened (e.g. a passport with a 180-day reminder). Sorted by due date, with today's date stated. This is the main 'what's coming up?' tool.

tools.name: add_item
tools.description: Start tracking something: a bill, renewal, subscription, warranty, policy, vehicle or document. Use only facts the user gave you; leave out a due date or cost rather than guessing. Refuses an exact duplicate title (use update_item instead) and anything that looks like a full card number.

title.description: Short, specific name, e.g. 'Car insurance' or 'Boiler warranty'

type.description: What kind of thing it is

provider.description: Who it is with, e.g. 'Octopus Energy'

cost.description: Cost per period as the user stated it (for income: the amount received). Never estimate.

due.description: Next renewal, payment or expiry date as YYYY-MM-DD. Only a date the user gave you.

remind_days.description: Days before due to start reminding (default 14)

auto_renews.description: True if it renews or charges automatically unless stopped

ref.description: Policy, account or order reference; only the last four are kept

notes.description: Anything else worth keeping, in the user's words

tools.name: update_item
tools.description: Change fields on an existing item; anything you leave out stays as it is. `clear` removes a field. `add_note` appends a dated line to the item's history. For a renewal or payment that has been dealt with, use mark_handled instead so the due date moves on.

provider.description: Who it is with, e.g. 'Octopus Energy'

cost.description: Cost per period as the user stated it (for income: the amount received). Never estimate.

due.description: Next renewal, payment or expiry date as YYYY-MM-DD. Only a date the user gave you.

remind_days.description: Days before due to start reminding (default 14)

auto_renews.description: True if it renews or charges automatically unless stopped

ref.description: Policy, account or order reference; only the last four are kept

add_note.description: Append a dated line to the history

tools.name: mark_handled
tools.description: Record that the user has dealt with an item (renewed, paid, switched, replaced). Logs it in the item's history and moves the due date on: repeating items roll forward by their period (keeping month-end dates right), `next_due` sets a date explicitly, and a one-off item's due date is cleared. Pass `new_cost` when the price changed; the old and new prices are logged.

note.description: What was done, e.g. 'Renewed with Admiral after haggling'

new_cost.description: The new cost per period, if it changed

next_due.description: Set the next due date explicitly (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: export_calendar
tools.description: Write every item that has a due date to an .ics file the user can import into Apple Calendar, Google Calendar or Outlook. Each item becomes an all-day event with a 9am reminder when its reminder window opens and another on the day; repeating items repeat in the calendar. After changes, export again and import into the same calendar to update the events. Provider and cost are included unless `minimal` is true; references and notes never are. Calendars often sync to a cloud account, so tell the user that.

minimal.description: Leave out provider and cost (titles and dates only)

tools.name: delete_item
tools.description: Stop tracking an item. It moves to the trash and can be brought back with restore_item. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: restore_item
tools.description: Bring back the most recently deleted item with this title.

tools.name: import_bank_file
tools.description: Read a bank statement exported as CSV (every UK bank app can export one) and add its transactions to the person's spending records, sorted into categories. Always run first with confirm false to show a preview, then again with confirm true once the person agrees. Already-imported lines are skipped, so overlapping statements are safe. The file stays on this computer.

path.description: Full path to the .csv file, e.g. ~/Downloads/statement.csv

tools.name: add_spending
tools.description: Record one payment or refund the person tells you about ("I spent £42 on a meal out"). The category is worked out from the description unless given. Amounts are always positive; set money_in for refunds or money received. Categories: bills (Bills & energy), groceries (Groceries), shopping (Shopping), going-out (Eating & going out), transport (Transport), tax (Tax), subscriptions (Subscriptions), savings (Savings), income (Income), transfers (Transfers), other (Other).

description.description: What or where, e.g. 'Meal out at The Red Lion'

money_in.description: True for a refund or money received

tools.name: categorise
tools.description: Put every transaction whose description contains these words (whole words, any case) into a category, and by default remember it so future imports are sorted the same way. Use after an import lists unsorted shops. Categories: bills (Bills & energy), groceries (Groceries), shopping (Shopping), going-out (Eating & going out), transport (Transport), tax (Tax), subscriptions (Subscriptions), savings (Savings), income (Income), transfers (Transfers), other (Other).

match.description: Words from the description, e.g. 'RED LION'

remember.description: Save as a rule for next time (default true)

tools.name: spending_summary
tools.description: What was spent this week or month by category, compared with what's usual for the person (the average of up to four earlier periods), plus money in, money saved and the biggest shops. Weeks run Monday to Sunday. offset 1 means last week/month.

tools.name: money_ahead
tools.description: Payments due between today and the next payday (from income items, moved to the working day before if payday falls on a weekend or bank holiday), with their total. Given the person's current balance, says roughly what is left until payday. Never guess the balance: ask for it.

balance.description: Current bank balance the person gave you

days.description: Look this many days ahead instead of to payday

tools.name: rainy_day_plan
tools.description: Work out how much the person could put aside, from their own income items and spending records: big yearly bills smoothed into monthly set-asides, then Gentle, Steady and Stretch options, each with a risk check against their tightest recent month and time to a £1,000 pot and to three months of essentials. Flags varying income, rising spending, big bills due soon and signs of borrowing. Arithmetic only: never recommend financial products, accounts or investments.

tools.name: update_pot
tools.description: Record what is in the rainy-day pot: set the amount saved, add to it (or take from it with a negative amount), or set a goal. Only use figures the person gave you.

saved.description: Set the amount saved so far

add.description: Add this much (negative to take some out)

tools.name: bank_holidays
tools.description: Upcoming UK bank holidays (official gov.uk list, bundled) for England and Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland. Useful because pay due on a bank holiday or weekend usually arrives the working day before, and payments due then are usually taken the next working day.

tools.name: open_home_screen
tools.description: Open the person's home screen in their web browser: what's coming up, the next payday and the bills before it, this week's spending and the rainy-day pot, in large, calm print with a Print button. It runs only on this computer, and stays available while this assistant session is open.

instructions: Local-first life admin: renewals, bills, subscriptions, warranties, policies, vehicles and documents, each stored as a markdown file on the user's own machine. Use due_soon to see what needs attention, add_item to track something new (search_items first to avoid duplicates), and mark_handled once the user has dealt with a renewal or payment. Store only the last four digits of any account or card number. Never invent dates or prices; ask the user. Nothing here sends reminders by itself: export_calendar puts due dates and reminders into the user's own calendar app, so never promise a reminder without it.
